title: A $639 Billion Bank Died Over One Weekend #shorts
description:
In September two thousand eight, Lehman Brothers, a bank that had survived for one hundred and fifty-eight years, filed the biggest bankruptcy in American history. Thirty to one leverage, an accounting trick and a weekend with no buyer.
Follow for more stories of money that vanished overnight.
hook_text:
A $639 BILLION BANK
DIED OVER ONE WEEKEND
first_comment: Should the government have saved Lehman, or was letting it fail the right call? 👇

lines.text: In two thousand eight, a bank with six hundred and thirty-nine billion dollars in assets died over one weekend.
The biggest bankruptcy in American history.
Lehman Brothers had survived one hundred and fifty-eight years.
But it had bet everything on American housing.
It borrowed about thirty dollars for every dollar it really had.
When home prices fell, its mortgage bonds started to rot.
To look safer, it used an accounting trick called Repo one-oh-five.
It quietly moved fifty billion dollars off its books, right before its reports.
Then came the final weekend. The government refused to save it, and every buyer walked away.
On Monday, September fifteenth, Lehman filed for bankruptcy.
Around twenty-five thousand employees carried their careers out in cardboard boxes.
And the whole world fell into a financial crisis.
Follow for more stories of money that vanished overnight.
